rapport.adapted_script: You're going in almost blind. All you have is a company name and a phone number. Your entire job on this call is DISCOVERY: is this a compressed-air distributor, what does he sell, and does he already carry a dryer/filtration line? Start by confirming you've reached the owner. Ask what the business does and how he handles air treatment on a compressor sale. Listen for 'drop-ship,' 'Kaishan,' 'we just buy whatever' — any of those is your opening. He's likely guarded and skeptical (he's been burned by a manufacturer before), so you have to earn the right to pitch. Don't propose the distributor program until you've confirmed he's a distributor, he's not locked to a brand, and you've heard the margin/lead-time pain in his own words.
watch_outs: No email on file — if you get one during the call, that's a win
No title — you don't even know for certain he's the decision maker; confirm it
Zero interaction history — he has never heard of KSI
Don't reference data you don't have — you'll sound like you're guessing. And SCOPE: KSI's line here is dryers and filtration ONLY
product_reference: ECOTROC KTA-S — refrigerated dryers, 14 to ~1,890 CFM, ~$1,880 up to ~$47,000. The everyday treatment attach if he'll carry a line.
ECOTROC DDAP — desiccant dryers for low-dewpoint / critical air. Higher ticket, higher margin.
ECOCLEAN APF — coalescing + particulate filtration, ~$155 to ~$709 per housing. Recurring consumable pull-through.
Positioning (only after you've confirmed he's a distributor who drop-ships): a treatment line he OWNS with real margin, plus KSI Midwest lead-feed and co-marketing.
German-engineered — reliability protects a service shop's reputation. Lead times and support are the objection under every other objection for this guy.
